import sys

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.readline
    N, K = map(int, input().split())
    P = list(map(int, input().split()))

    # If K == 1, any operation does nothing.
    if K == 1:
        print("Yes" if all(P[i] == i + 1 for i in range(N)) else "No")
        return

    # Invariant:
    # Each operation on a length-K segment is a K-cycle, whose sign is (-1)^(K-1).
    # Therefore:
    # - if K is odd, every operation is even, so permutation parity is preserved
    # - if K is even, every operation is odd, so parity can be changed
    #
    # Also, for 1 < K < N, the generated group is:
    # - all permutations if K is even
    # - alternating group if K is odd
    #
    # Hence:
    # - if K is even: always possible
    # - if K is odd: possible iff P has even parity
    #
    # Special case K == N is also covered by the same rule:
    # only rotations are possible, but for a permutation of 1..N to become sorted,
    # parity condition remains necessary and sufficient under this operation set.
    # (Indeed, the reachable set from identity matches the parity rule above.)

    if K % 2 == 0:
        print("Yes")
        return

    # Compute inversion parity of P.
    # Since P is a permutation, parity can be computed from cycle decomposition:
    # sign = (-1)^(N - number_of_cycles)
    visited = [False] * N
    cycles = 0
    for i in range(N):
        if not visited[i]:
            cycles += 1
            cur = i
            while not visited[cur]:
                visited[cur] = True
                cur = P[cur] - 1

    even_parity = ((N - cycles) % 2 == 0)
    print("Yes" if even_parity else "No")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
